frosh-tools.title: Tools

index.title: System status
index.subtitle: Live health and performance checks for this Shopware instance.

ioncube-loader.title: ionCube Loader can drastically decrease performance

multiple-autoloaders.title: Composer autoloaders
multiple-autoloaders.description: More than one Composer autoloader is registered in the running process. This usually happens when a plugin ships its own "vendor/" directory: its dependencies get loaded a second time, Composer can no longer track installed versions reliably, and you can run into duplicate-class or wrong-version bugs that are hard to diagnose.
multiple-autoloaders.solution: Remove the bundled "vendor/" directories so only the project autoloader is used. If a plugin requires its own dependencies, ask its author to declare them as Composer requirements instead of shipping a vendor folder.

queue.title: Open Queues
queue.description: Messages have been waiting in a monitored messenger queue longer than the configured grace time. That almost always means no worker is consuming that queue, so asynchronous tasks (mails, indexing, …) pile up. Failed queues (names containing "failed") are ignored by default because they are usually drained manually.
queue.solution: Make sure a CLI worker is running and supervised (e.g. via systemd or Supervisor) so the queue is drained continuously. Adjust monitored queues and per-queue grace times under Settings → Extensions → Frosh Tools if needed.

adapter.title: Queue transport
adapter.description: The message queue uses a transport that is not suited for production. The database (doctrine) transport does not scale well once multiple workers consume it, and the "sync" transport executes jobs inside the web request instead of in the background.
adapter.solution: Use a dedicated queue backend such as Redis or RabbitMQ for the messenger transport.

symfony_scheduler.title: Symfony scheduler overdue
symfony_scheduler.description: A symfony/scheduler schedule has not dispatched the message that was already due, or has never dispatched anything at all. Each schedule is consumed through its own messenger transport named "scheduler_<name>", which is separate from the regular queues — a worker consuming only "async" will not run it. The check compares the schedule's stored checkpoint with the first message due after it, so a task that simply runs weekly is not reported.
symfony_scheduler.solution: Run a supervised CLI worker for the scheduler transport of every schedule. The grace time is shared with the scheduled task check under Settings → Extensions → Frosh Tools.

mysql-timezone.title: MySQL Time Zone Support
mysql-timezone.description: The MySQL time zone tables are not loaded, so CONVERT_TZ() and named time zones (e.g. "Europe/Berlin") do not work. Features that rely on time zone conversion can silently return wrong results.
mysql-timezone.solution: Import the zoneinfo data into MySQL once on the database server:

security-eol-shopware.title: Security updates
security-eol-shopware.description: Your Shopware version is approaching, or has already passed, its security end-of-life. Once security support ends you no longer receive security fixes, which is a real risk for a production shop.
security-eol-shopware.solution: Plan an update to a still-supported version, ideally the latest LTS release.

system-time.title: System time offset
system-time.description: The server clock differs noticeably from real time. A drifting clock breaks time-sensitive features such as TOTP/2FA, OAuth tokens, scheduled tasks and signed requests.
system-time.solution: Enable automatic time synchronisation (NTP/chrony) on the host so the system clock stays accurate.

php-fpm-max-listen-queue.title: PHP FPM max listen queue
php-fpm-max-listen-queue.description: Requests have had to wait in the PHP-FPM listen queue because no worker was free. A value above 0 indicates the pool is occasionally too small for your peak load.
php-fpm-max-listen-queue.solution: Increase the number of PHP-FPM workers (pm.max_children and the related pm.* settings) for the pool, making sure the host has enough memory for the extra workers.

php-fpm-max-children-reached.title: PHP FPM max children reached
php-fpm-max-children-reached.description: PHP-FPM has hit its pm.max_children limit, meaning all workers were busy and additional requests had to wait. A value above 0 points to a pool that is too small for peak traffic.
php-fpm-max-children-reached.solution: Raise pm.max_children for the FPM pool (and verify the host has enough RAM to back the additional workers).

php-fpm-memory-peak.title: PHP FPM memory peak
php-fpm-memory-peak.description: The highest amount of memory a single PHP-FPM worker has used. This is informational — use it to size memory_limit and to decide how many workers (pm.max_children) fit into the available RAM.

shopware-installer.title: Shopware installer
shopware-installer.description: The Shopware web installer (shopware-installer.phar.php) is still in the public directory. Anyone who can request that URL can start a reinstall and overwrite the shop, so it is a security risk to leave it there after installation.
shopware-installer.solution: Delete public/shopware-installer.phar.php from the shop. The installer is only needed during the initial setup and must not stay publicly accessible.

composer-conflicts-repository.title: Composer conflicts repository
composer-conflicts-repository.description: The Shopware conflicts repository (https://shopware.github.io/conflicts/) is not registered in the "repositories" section of your root composer.json. This repository declares combinations of packages and versions that are known to be incompatible. With it in place, Composer refuses to install or update to a broken combination before it reaches production; without it those guard rails are missing.
composer-conflicts-repository.solution: Add the conflicts repository to the "repositories" section of your root composer.json (either edit the file directly or run the composer command below), then run "composer update" so Composer re-evaluates your dependencies against it.

admin-watcher.title: Admin-Worker
admin-watcher.description: The admin worker processes the message queue from within the administration in the browser and keeps a request open for every logged-in admin user. It does not scale and competes with regular traffic.
admin-watcher.solution: Disable the admin worker and run the queue via supervised CLI workers instead.

cache-compression-method.description: Cache entries are compressed with gzip. zstd compresses faster and produces smaller payloads, which lowers both CPU usage and the size stored in the cache backend.
cache-compression-method.solution: Switch the cache compression method to zstd (requires the PHP "zstd" extension).

cart-compression-method.description: The cart is compressed with gzip. zstd compresses faster and produces smaller payloads, lowering CPU usage and the storage footprint of persisted carts.
cart-compression-method.solution: Switch the cart compression method to zstd (requires the PHP "zstd" extension).

cache-compression-method-extension-zstd.description: The cache compression method is set to zstd, but the PHP "zstd" extension is not installed. Compression will fail until the extension is available.
cache-compression-method-extension-zstd.solution: Install and enable the PHP zstd extension, or switch the compression method back to gzip.

cart-compression-method-extension-zstd.description: The cart compression method is set to zstd, but the PHP "zstd" extension is not installed. Compression will fail until the extension is available.
cart-compression-method-extension-zstd.solution: Install and enable the PHP zstd extension, or switch the compression method back to gzip.

app-url-check-disabled.title: App URL external check
app-url-check-disabled.description: On every request Shopware verifies that the configured APP_URL matches the incoming request. On a correctly configured host this check is redundant and only adds overhead.
app-url-check-disabled.solution: Disable the external APP_URL check via an environment variable once you are sure APP_URL is configured correctly.

symfony-secrets.title: Disable Symfony Secrets
symfony-secrets.description: Symfony's secrets vault is initialised on every request. If you do not use encrypted Symfony secrets, disabling the vault removes that per-request overhead.
symfony-secrets.solution: Disable the secrets vault if you do not rely on it.

mail_variables.title: MailVariables updates
mail_variables.description: By default Shopware writes mail template variables back to the database after each mail is sent. On shops that send many mails this causes a noticeable amount of extra write load.
mail_variables.solution: Disable updating mail variables on send.

elasticsearch.title: Elasticsearch
elasticsearch.description: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch is not enabled. For larger catalogs it offloads search and listing queries from MySQL, which significantly improves response times and reduces database load.
elasticsearch.solution: Set up an Elasticsearch/OpenSearch server and enable it via the environment, then build the index.

fine-grained-caching.title: Fine-grained caching on Redis, Varnish etc.
fine-grained-caching.description: Fine-grained cache tagging creates a separate cache tag for every config, snippet and theme config value. With Redis or Varnish this bloats tag storage and makes invalidation more expensive.

cache-id.title: Fixed cache id
cache-id.description: No fixed cache id is set. Without it the cache namespace changes on every deployment or cache clear, so caches cannot be reused across deployments or shared between cluster nodes.
cache-id.solution: Set a stable SHOPWARE_CACHE_ID (identical across all nodes of a cluster). Note: this setting was removed in Shopware 6.7.

increment-storage.title: Increment storage
increment-storage.description: The increment storage (user activity and message-queue statistics) is backed by MySQL, which generates a large number of small writes. Using "array" or Redis scales much better.
increment-storage.solution: Move the increment storage to Redis (or "array" if you do not need it persisted).

business_logger.title: BusinessEventHandler logging
business_logger.description: The business event handler logs below WARNING level. On a busy shop this writes a large volume of low-value log entries, adding I/O and storage overhead.
business_logger.solution: Raise the business event handler log level to at least WARNING via your Monolog configuration.

mail.title: Sending mails over queue
mail.description: Mails are sent synchronously during the request. The customer then has to wait for the SMTP server to respond. Routing mail through the message queue sends it in the background.
mail.solution: Route the SendEmailMessage onto the asynchronous transport so mails are delivered by the worker.

messenger-auto-setup.title: Messenger auto_setup
messenger-auto-setup.description: The messenger transport has auto_setup enabled, so it checks (and potentially creates) its queue/table on every connect. On production this is unnecessary overhead.
messenger-auto-setup.solution: Append "auto_setup=false" to the transport DSN(s) and create the transports once via the console.

sql_group_concat_max_len.title: MySQL value group_concat_max_len
sql_group_concat_max_len.description: MySQL's group_concat_max_len is too low. Shopware aggregates data with GROUP_CONCAT and a low limit silently truncates the result, which leads to broken data or errors.
sql_group_concat_max_len.solution: Raise group_concat_max_len on the MySQL server.

sql_mode.title: MySQL value sql_mode
sql_mode.description: MySQL's sql_mode contains ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY, which rejects some of the grouped queries Shopware relies on and can cause runtime errors.
sql_mode.solution: Remove ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY from the server sql_mode.

sql_time_zone.title: MySQL value time_zone
sql_time_zone.description: The database is not running in UTC. Shopware stores timestamps in UTC, so a different database time zone leads to wrong dates and times. (Relevant before Shopware 6.7.)
sql_time_zone.solution: Set the MySQL time_zone to UTC.

sql_set_default_session_variables.title: MySQL session vars are set on each connect
sql_set_default_session_variables.description: Shopware sets default session variables on every new database connection, adding a round-trip per connect. Configuring the equivalents on the server avoids this. (Relevant before Shopware 6.7.)
sql_set_default_session_variables.solution: Disable the per-connect session variables and apply the equivalent settings in your MySQL server configuration instead.

enable_file_override.title: PHP value opcache.enable_file_override
enable_file_override.description: opcache.enable_file_override lets OPcache answer file_exists()/is_file()/is_readable() from the cache, reducing filesystem calls on every request.
enable_file_override.solution: Enable it in your PHP configuration.

interned_strings_buffer.title: PHP value opcache.interned_strings_buffer
interned_strings_buffer.description: The OPcache interned strings buffer is small. Shopware uses a lot of strings, so a small buffer reduces OPcache efficiency and increases memory churn.
interned_strings_buffer.solution: Increase the interned strings buffer in your PHP configuration.

detect_unicode.title: PHP value zend.detect_unicode
detect_unicode.description: zend.detect_unicode makes PHP scan the beginning of every file for a BOM. Disabling it avoids that unnecessary work.
detect_unicode.solution: Disable it in your PHP configuration.

realpath_cache_ttl.title: PHP value realpath_cache_ttl
realpath_cache_ttl.description: A low realpath_cache_ttl causes PHP to re-resolve and stat file paths frequently, increasing filesystem load on every request.
realpath_cache_ttl.solution: Increase the realpath cache TTL in your PHP configuration.

assertions.title: PHP value zend.assertions
assertions.description: Assertions should be compiled out in production. Any value other than -1 means assertion code is still compiled and executed, wasting CPU.
assertions.solution: Disable assertions in your production PHP configuration.

product-stream-indexing.title: Product Stream Indexing
product-stream-indexing.description: Product stream indexing keeps a pre-computed mapping of products to dynamic product groups up to date. On many shops this background work is unnecessary and can be disabled.
product-stream-indexing.solution: Disable product stream indexing if you do not depend on the pre-computed mapping.

redis-tag-aware.title: HTTP cache (cache.http) Redis adapter should be TagAware
redis-tag-aware.description: This check looks at the HTTP cache pool (cache.http) only — not cache.object or other pools. The plain Redis adapter stores cache tags inefficiently; RedisTagAware is optimised for Shopware’s tag-based HTTP cache invalidation. Using plain Redis for cache.object on purpose is fine and will not trigger this warning.
redis-tag-aware.solution: Configure the HTTP cache pool (or the default app adapter that cache.http inherits) to use the TagAware Redis adapter.

data-integrity.title: Data integrity
data-integrity.subtitle: Inconsistent shop data that Shopware accepts but that causes problems in the storefront.

affected.title: Affected records
affected.loadError: The affected records could not be loaded.
affected.empty: No affected records found. Refresh the checks to update the count.
affected.unavailable: This check cannot list the affected records.
affected.forbidden: You are not allowed to view these records.

product-canonical-without-variants.title: Products without variants that have a canonical product
product-canonical-without-variants.description: A product without variants has a canonical product set. The canonical product selects which variant of a product is used as the canonical URL, so on a product without variants it is a leftover, for example from variants that were deleted later. It can point search engines to a URL that no longer belongs to this product.
product-canonical-without-variants.solution: The SEO tab of the administration only offers the canonical product for products with variants, so remove it through the Admin API by setting "canonicalProductId" to null, for example with an import.

product-canonical-other-family.title: Products with a canonical product of another product
product-canonical-other-family.description: The canonical product of these products is not one of their own variants but belongs to another product. Search engines are told that the page is a duplicate of a different product, so the product page can drop out of the search index.
product-canonical-other-family.solution: Open the product in the administration and select one of its own variants as canonical product in the SEO tab, or remove the canonical product.

product-main-variant-invalid.title: Products with a main variant that is missing or of another product
product-main-variant-invalid.description: The main variant configured for the product listing does not exist anymore or is not a variant of this product. The listing then cannot show the intended variant for the product.
product-main-variant-invalid.solution: Open the product in the administration and select one of its own variants as main variant in the variants tab under "Storefront presentation".

variant-main-variant-config.title: Variants with their own main variant configuration
variant-main-variant-config.description: A variant has its own main variant configuration. The main variant is configured on the main product and applies to all of its variants, a value on a variant is a leftover, for example from a product that was converted into a variant.
variant-main-variant-config.solution: Remove the main variant configuration from these variants, so they inherit the configuration of their main product.

product-description-too-long.title: Product descriptions longer than 32766 bytes
product-description-too-long.description: Elasticsearch rejects single terms larger than 32766 bytes. Before Shopware 6.6.6.0 the product description was indexed as such a term, so products with a longer description fail to index and are missing from search and listings.
product-description-too-long.solution: Shorten the descriptions, or update Shopware to 6.6.6.0 or later, which no longer indexes long values as a single term.

duplicate-delivery-times.title: Delivery times with the same range and unit
duplicate-delivery-times.description: Several delivery times have the same minimum, maximum and unit. They are shown identically in the storefront, but rules, filters and imports that refer to one of them miss the products using the others.
duplicate-delivery-times.solution: Assign the products and shipping methods of the duplicates to one of the delivery times and delete the others.

duplicate-customer-emails.title: Customers sharing an email address
duplicate-customer-emails.description: Several registered customers share an email address, although Shopware requires it to be unique per sales channel when customers are bound to their sales channel, and unique across all sales channels otherwise. The login always uses the newest of these accounts, so the customers of the older accounts cannot log in anymore.
duplicate-customer-emails.solution: Merge or delete the duplicate customer accounts, or change their email addresses. Guest accounts are not counted.

product-cover-invalid.title: Products with a missing cover or the cover of another product
product-cover-invalid.description: The cover of these products points to an image that was deleted or that belongs to another product. "product.product_media_id" has no foreign key, so deleting the image leaves the reference behind. Listings and the product page then show no image or the image of another product. A cover of another product that shows the same image as one of the product's own images is not counted, because it displays correctly.
product-cover-invalid.solution: Open the product in the administration and select a cover in the media tab.

variant-duplicate-options.title: Variants with the same options as another variant
variant-duplicate-options.description: Several variants of a product have exactly the same options. The variant switcher in the storefront can only reach one of them, so the others cannot be selected and their stock is not sold.
variant-duplicate-options.solution: Delete the surplus variants in the variants tab of the main product, after moving their stock, prices and media to the variant that remains. Inactive variants are not counted, because the variant selection does not offer them.

variant-without-options.title: Variants without options
variant-without-options.description: These variants have no options at all, usually because they were imported without them or the options were deleted. The variant switcher cannot select them.
variant-without-options.solution: Delete these variants and generate them again in the variants tab of the main product, or assign their options through the Admin API.

product-delivery-time-missing.title: Products with a delivery time that does not exist
product-delivery-time-missing.description: These products refer to a delivery time that was deleted. "product.delivery_time_id" has no foreign key, so the reference stays behind and no delivery time is shown for the product.
product-delivery-time-missing.solution: Select an existing delivery time in the deliverability section of the product.

product-layout-wrong-type.title: Products with a layout that is not a product page layout
product-layout-wrong-type.description: These products use a layout that is not a product page layout, for example a listing or landing page layout. Such layouts lack the product specific elements like the buy box.
product-layout-wrong-type.solution: Assign a product page layout in the layout tab of the product, or remove the layout to use the default one.

category-layout-wrong-type.title: Categories with a product page layout
category-layout-wrong-type.description: These categories use a product page layout, which expects a product and cannot render a category page.
category-layout-wrong-type.solution: Assign a listing, landing page or shop page layout in the layout tab of the category.

rule-invalid.title: Rules with invalid conditions
rule-invalid.description: Shopware marks a rule as invalid when one of its conditions cannot be loaded anymore, usually because the extension that provided it was removed. Invalid rules are never loaded into the cart, so prices, shipping methods, payment methods and promotions that depend on them stop working.
rule-invalid.solution: Open the rules in the rule builder and replace the missing conditions, or reinstall the extension that provided them.

flow-invalid.title: Active flows with invalid actions
flow-invalid.description: Shopware marks a flow as invalid when one of its actions cannot be loaded anymore, usually because the extension that provided it was removed. Invalid flows are skipped, so their mails and other actions are not executed even though the flow is active.
flow-invalid.solution: Open the flows in the flow builder and replace the missing actions, or reinstall the extension that provided them.

product-stream-invalid.title: Dynamic product groups with invalid filters
product-stream-invalid.description: Shopware marks a dynamic product group as invalid when its filters cannot be converted into a search, for example because a filtered field or custom field no longer exists. Core throws an error for such a group, so category listings, cross selling, product sliders and product exports that use it fail.
product-stream-invalid.solution: Open the dynamic product groups and fix or remove the broken filters.

sales-channel-default-payment-unassigned.title: Sales channels whose default payment method is not assigned
sales-channel-default-payment-unassigned.description: The default payment method of these sales channels is not one of their assigned payment methods. New carts still start with the default payment method, which the sales channel does not offer, so the cart reports it as blocked: the storefront switches to another payment method and shows a notice, headless clients have to switch it themselves. The administration prevents this, so it usually comes from imports or API writes.
sales-channel-default-payment-unassigned.solution: Assign the default payment method to the sales channel or choose one of the assigned methods as default.

sales-channel-default-shipping-unassigne.title: Sales channels whose default shipping method is not assigned
sales-channel-default-shipping-unassigne.description: The default shipping method of these sales channels is not one of their assigned shipping methods. New carts still start with the default shipping method, which the sales channel does not offer, so the cart reports it as blocked: the storefront switches to another shipping method and shows a notice, headless clients have to switch it themselves. The administration prevents this, so it usually comes from imports or API writes.
sales-channel-default-shipping-unassigne.solution: Assign the default shipping method to the sales channel or choose one of the assigned methods as default.

sales-channel-domain-language-unassigned.title: Domains with a language that is not assigned to their sales channel
sales-channel-domain-language-unassigned.description: These domains use a language that is not assigned to their sales channel. Features that are based on the assigned languages, like the language switcher, do not cover the domain. The administration only offers assigned languages, so it usually comes from imports or API writes.
sales-channel-domain-language-unassigned.solution: Assign the language to the sales channel or change the language of the domain.

sales-channel-domain-currency-unassigned.title: Domains with a currency that is not assigned to their sales channel
sales-channel-domain-currency-unassigned.description: These domains use a currency that is not assigned to their sales channel. Features that are based on the assigned currencies, like the currency switcher, do not cover the domain. The administration only offers assigned currencies, so it usually comes from imports or API writes.
sales-channel-domain-currency-unassigned.solution: Assign the currency to the sales channel or change the currency of the domain.

shipping-method-without-prices.title: Active shipping methods without prices
shipping-method-without-prices.description: These shipping methods are active but have no price matrix. Their shipping costs cannot be calculated, so they cannot be used in the checkout.
shipping-method-without-prices.solution: Add prices to the shipping methods or deactivate them.

customer-default-address-invalid.title: Customers with a missing default address or the address of another customer
customer-default-address-invalid.description: The default billing or shipping address of these customers does not exist or belongs to another customer. The default address columns have no foreign keys, so deleted or reassigned addresses stay referenced. Checkout and account pages expect both addresses and can fail for these customers.
customer-default-address-invalid.solution: Select existing addresses of the customer as default billing and shipping address in the customer detail page. Guest accounts are not counted.

category-sorting-invalid.title: Categories sorted after a category of another parent
category-sorting-invalid.description: These categories are sorted after a category that has another parent. The position of a category is stored as the sibling it follows, so the sorting of the category tree breaks for them.
category-sorting-invalid.solution: Drag the categories to their intended position in the category tree of the administration, which stores a valid sibling.

sales-channel-navigation-category-inacti.title: Storefronts with an inactive main navigation category
sales-channel-navigation-category-inacti.description: The main navigation category of these active storefront sales channels is inactive. The storefront loads this category as homepage and answers with a 404 error when it is inactive, so the homepage of the shop cannot be reached.
sales-channel-navigation-category-inacti.solution: Activate the category in the category tree of the administration, or select an active category as main navigation in the settings of the sales channel.

system-config-cms-page-missing.title: Shop pages and default layouts pointing to deleted layouts
system-config-cms-page-missing.description: A shop page selected in the basic information settings, for example terms and conditions, privacy, imprint, 404 or maintenance page, or a default layout for products or categories points to a layout that no longer exists. Links to these shop pages lead to an error page, a missing 404 page turns every 404 error into a server error with status 500, and a missing maintenance page breaks the maintenance mode. Without the default product layout, product pages without their own layout are rendered without any layout, and without the default category layout, category pages without their own layout can fail on Shopware 6.6.
system-config-cms-page-missing.solution: Select an existing layout for these pages in the basic information settings, globally and in every sales channel that overrides them, and set an existing layout as default for products and categories in Shopping Experiences.

product-stream-without-filters-in-use.title: Dynamic product groups without filters that are still in use
product-stream-without-filters-in-use.description: These dynamic product groups have no valid filters, because all filters were removed or the filters are invalid, but they are still used by a category, an active cross-selling, a product comparison or a product slider in a layout. Shopware throws an error instead of showing products, so the category, product or layout page fails to load and the product comparison cannot be generated.
product-stream-without-filters-in-use.solution: Add valid filters to the dynamic product groups and save them, or remove them from the categories, cross-sellings, product comparisons and layouts that use them.

product-display-group-missing.title: Products hidden from listings by a missing display group
product-display-group-missing.description: These products or variants have no display group. Listings, search and product sliders only show products with a display group, so these products are missing there although they are active and visible. This happens when products are imported directly into the database without running the indexer afterwards, or when a variant has no option of a property group that is expanded in the variant listing configuration of its main product.
product-display-group-missing.solution: Assign the missing option to the variant or change the variant listing configuration of the main product if needed, then rebuild the product index with "bin/console dal:refresh:index --only=product.indexer" or in the administration under Settings, System, Caches and indexes.

payment-method-handler-missing.title: Active payment methods without an available payment handler
payment-method-handler-missing.description: These payment methods are active and assigned to a sales channel, but their payment handler is gone, usually because the plugin that provided it was deactivated or removed, or the app was deleted. Customers can still select them. For payment methods of plugins, placing an order fails with an unknown payment method error. For payment methods of deleted apps, the order is created, but the payment fails.
payment-method-handler-missing.solution: Reactivate or reinstall the plugin or app that provides the payment methods, or deactivate the payment methods and remove them from the sales channels.

delivery-time-invalid.title: Delivery times with an unsupported unit or a negative duration
delivery-time-invalid.description: These delivery times use a unit Shopware does not support, only hour, day, week, month and year in lowercase are valid, or they have a negative minimum or maximum. Shopware cannot calculate a delivery date from them, so the cart calculation fails with an error for line items with such a delivery time, and for line items without their own delivery time when the selected shipping method has one. The administration only offers valid values, so they usually come from imports or API writes.
delivery-time-invalid.solution: Open the delivery times in the administration settings and select a valid unit and non-negative minimum and maximum values.

currency-rounding-interval-zero.title: Currency roundings with an interval of zero
currency-rounding-interval-zero.description: The item or total rounding of these currencies or country specific currency roundings has an interval of zero or no interval, with at most two decimal places. Shopware divides by the interval when rounding prices, so every cart calculation in this currency fails with a division by zero error, for a country specific rounding only for customers from that country.
currency-rounding-interval-zero.solution: Open the currency in the administration and set a rounding interval greater than zero, for example 0.01, for the item and the total rounding, also in the country specific roundings of the currency.

currency-factor-invalid.title: Currencies with an invalid exchange rate factor
currency-factor-invalid.description: These currencies have an exchange rate factor of zero or below, or they are the default currency and their factor is not 1. Prices without an explicit value in a currency are converted with its factor, so a factor of zero or below results in free or negative prices. Shopware expects the default currency to have the factor 1, otherwise for example shipping costs in the default currency are multiplied by the factor and charged wrongly.
currency-factor-invalid.solution: Open the currencies in the administration and enter a positive factor, and set the factor of the default currency to 1.

tax-provider-unavailable.title: Active tax providers that are not available
tax-provider-unavailable.description: These tax providers are active, but no tax provider with their identifier is registered and they are not handled by an app, usually because the plugin that provided them was deactivated or removed. Shopware then reports an error for the missing tax provider, so the cart calculation fails unless a tax provider with a higher priority already provided the taxes.
tax-provider-unavailable.solution: Reactivate or reinstall the plugin that provides the tax providers, or deactivate the tax providers in the tax settings of the administration.

country-forced-state-without-states.title: Countries requiring a state without active states
country-forced-state-without-states.description: These countries are active, assigned to a sales channel and require a state for addresses, but have no active state. Customers cannot select a state for an address in this country, and the cart blocks orders whose billing or shipping address is in this country because the state is missing.
country-forced-state-without-states.solution: Add or activate the states of the country in the administration, or disable the setting that requires a state for this country.

sales-channel-default-country-unavailabl.title: Sales channels whose default country is not available for shipping
sales-channel-default-country-unavailabl.description: The default country of these active storefront or headless sales channels is inactive, not available for shipping or not assigned to the sales channel. Carts of visitors who are not logged in use the default country as shipping location, so the cart reports shipping to this country as blocked, and orders cannot be placed until the customer uses an address in a deliverable country.
sales-channel-default-country-unavailabl.solution: Choose an active, deliverable country that is assigned to the sales channel as its default country, or activate the country, allow shipping to it and assign it to the sales channel.

promotion-discount-setgroup-missing.title: Promotion discounts referencing a missing set group
promotion-discount-setgroup-missing.description: These discounts of active promotions apply to a set group by its position, but the promotion has no set group at that position, usually because set groups were deleted after the discount was configured. As soon as the cart fulfils all set groups of the promotion, the cart calculation fails with a set group not found error. A promotion without any set group never applies such a discount.
promotion-discount-setgroup-missing.solution: Open the promotion in the administration and select one of the existing set groups as scope of the discount, or add the missing set group again.

customer-requested-group-missing.title: Customers requesting a customer group that does not exist
customer-requested-group-missing.description: These customers requested a customer group that has been deleted. The column has no foreign key, so deleting the group does not reset the request. The administration notification for open customer group requests fails on login, and accepting or declining the request fails with an error.
customer-requested-group-missing.solution: Remove the requested customer group from these customers in the database, or create the customer group again and process the requests.

language-translation-code-missing.title: Languages without their own or an inherited translation code
language-translation-code-missing.description: These languages have no translation code, and neither has their parent language. Shopware uses the translation code to find the locale of a language, for example for mails, snippets and product exports, and fails with an error for these languages.
language-translation-code-missing.solution: Select a translation code for these languages or their parent language in the language settings.

product-price-tiers-invalid.title: Products with gaps or overlaps in their advanced prices
product-price-tiers-invalid.description: The advanced prices of these products do not form a continuous scale for at least one rule: the first tier does not start at quantity 1, a tier ends before it starts, or tiers leave a gap or overlap. The cart selects the tier only by the end quantity of the sorted tiers, so customers can be charged a different price than the price table on the product page shows.
product-price-tiers-invalid.solution: Open the product in the administration and adjust the advanced prices in the prices tab so that the first tier starts at 1 and every further tier starts directly after the end of the previous one.

product-max-purchase-below-min-purchase.title: Products with a maximum order quantity below the minimum order quantity
product-max-purchase-below-min-purchase.description: The maximum order quantity of these products, including a value inherited from the main product or, without any value, the maximum quantity per product from the cart settings, is lower than their minimum order quantity. The product page still shows the buy button, but the cart removes the product right away with an out of stock message, so it cannot be ordered.
product-max-purchase-below-min-purchase.solution: Open the product in the administration and set a maximum order quantity that is at least the minimum order quantity, or remove the maximum order quantity.

media-folder-configuration-missing.title: Media folders with a deleted folder configuration
media-folder-configuration-missing.description: These media folders refer to a folder configuration that no longer exists. The reference has no foreign key, so it is left behind when the configuration is deleted. Shopware then generates no thumbnails for new media in these folders, and regenerating thumbnails, for example with "bin/console media:generate-thumbnails", deletes the existing ones, so the storefront loads the full-size images.
media-folder-configuration-missing.solution: Assign an existing folder configuration to the media folder through the Admin API by setting "configurationId" before regenerating thumbnails, then generate the thumbnails again with "bin/console media:generate-thumbnails".

category-link-target-invalid.title: Link categories without a valid link target
category-link-target-invalid.description: These categories of type link have no usable target: the linked product, category or landing page was deleted, no internal target is selected, or an external link has no URL. Internal link targets have no foreign key, so deleting the target leaves the reference behind. The menu entry leads to a 404 page or to no page at all.
category-link-target-invalid.solution: Open the category in the administration and select an existing link target or enter a URL, or change the category type.

product-export-currency-invalid.title: Product comparisons with a missing or unassigned currency
product-export-currency-invalid.description: The currency of these product comparisons was deleted, or, since Shopware 6.7.15.0, is not assigned to the storefront sales channel the comparison is based on. The currency reference has no foreign key, so it is left behind when the currency is deleted. Generating the product comparison fails because the currency cannot be found, so the feed is not updated anymore.
product-export-currency-invalid.solution: Open the product comparison sales channel in the administration and select a currency that is assigned to its storefront sales channel, or assign the currency to the storefront sales channel.

product-configurator-settings-missing.title: Products with variants but without variant configurator settings
product-configurator-settings-missing.description: These main products have variants with options, but no configurator settings, so the product page shows no variant selection and customers cannot switch between the variants. This can be intended, for example when the variants are listed as separate products. Otherwise it usually happens when variants are imported without configurator settings.
product-configurator-settings-missing.solution: Create the configurator settings through the Admin API by adding the options of the variants to "configuratorSettings" of the main product. If the variants are intentionally sold without a variant selection, disable this check with the id "product-configurator-settings-missing" in "frosh_tools.checker.disabled_checks".

variant-option-configurator-setting-miss.title: Variants with options missing in the configurator settings
variant-option-configurator-setting-miss.description: These variants have options that are missing in the configurator settings of their main product. Before Shopware 6.7.14.0 the variant selection on the product page only offers configured options, so these variants cannot be selected and other options can appear as unavailable.
variant-option-configurator-setting-miss.solution: Add the missing options to "configuratorSettings" of the main product through the Admin API, or update Shopware to 6.7.14.0 or later, which also offers options without a configurator setting.

product-main-category-invalid.title: Main categories that cannot be used for the product
product-main-category-invalid.description: The main category selected for these products in a sales channel is not assigned to the product, is inactive, hidden on Shopware 6.7.9 to 6.7.14, or is not part of the navigation, service or footer category tree of that sales channel. The breadcrumb ignores such a main category and falls back to another category, while SEO URL templates that use the main category still use it, so URL and breadcrumb can disagree. Before Shopware 6.7.9 an inactive main category is still used, so the breadcrumb links to a category page that cannot be opened.
product-main-category-invalid.solution: Open the product in the administration and select an assigned, active category of the sales channel as main category in the SEO tab, or assign and activate the category.

product-without-visible-category.title: Active products without an active and visible category in the sales channel
product-without-visible-category.description: These products are active and visible in listings and search of a sales channel, but none of their categories is active, visible in the navigation and part of the navigation, service or footer category tree of that sales channel. Customers can still find them through the search or a direct link, but no category page lists them, and the breadcrumb and SEO URLs have no category to use. Categories that show the product through a dynamic product group are not considered.
product-without-visible-category.solution: Open the product in the administration and assign an active, visible category of the sales channel, activate or show one of its categories, or hide the product in listings and search of the sales channel in the visibility settings.

rule-condition-deleted-references.title: Rule conditions referencing only deleted entities
rule-condition-deleted-references.description: These rule conditions only reference payment methods, shipping methods, customer groups, countries, states, sales channels, currencies, languages, tags, salutations or dynamic product groups that were deleted. Shopware does not remove deleted entities from rule conditions, so a condition with is one of never matches and a condition with is none of always matches. Prices, shipping methods, payment methods, promotions and flows that depend on these rules behave differently than intended.
rule-condition-deleted-references.solution: Open the rules in the rule builder and select existing entities in the conditions, or remove the conditions.

rule-duplicate-conditions.title: Rules with identical conditions
rule-duplicate-conditions.description: These rules have the same conditions as at least one other rule. The order of the conditions and of the selected values is ignored, name, priority and assignments are not compared. Rules with identical conditions are listed next to each other, and each rule names the rules it shares its conditions with. Duplicates usually come from copied rules or from rules that were created again because the existing one was not found. They make it hard to see which rule a price, shipping method, payment method, promotion or flow depends on, and changes to one copy do not reach the others. A duplicate can be intended, for example to keep assignments separate.
rule-duplicate-conditions.solution: Keep one rule of each set, assign its prices, shipping methods, payment methods, promotions and flows to it in the Assignments tab of the rule builder, and delete the other rules.

flow-action-deleted-references.title: Active flow actions referencing deleted entities
flow-action-deleted-references.description: These actions of active flows reference a mail template, tag or customer group that was deleted. A send mail action with a deleted mail template is skipped without any error, so the mail is never sent. Adding a deleted tag or changing to a deleted customer group fails with an error, and the remaining actions of the flow are not executed.
flow-action-deleted-references.solution: Open the flows in the Flow Builder and select an existing mail template, tag or customer group in these actions, or remove the actions.

tax-rule-states-invalid.title: Tax rules for individual states that match no state of their country
tax-rule-states-invalid.description: These tax rules of the type individual states do not contain any state of their own country, for example because the states were deleted, the state ids are stored in uppercase, or the rule was copied to another country. Such a rule never applies, so customers from the intended states are silently charged the standard tax rate. Before Shopware 6.6.7, a rule without any states even makes the cart calculation fail with an error.
tax-rule-states-invalid.solution: Open the tax in the administration and select the intended states of the country in the tax rule, or delete the tax rule.

flow-mail-template-incomplete.title: Mail templates of active flows without a complete default translation
flow-mail-template-incomplete.description: These mail templates are sent by active flows, but their translation in the default language is missing or has an empty subject, HTML content or plain text content. Mails in languages without their own complete translation fall back to the default language, fail the validation of the mail service and are not sent. The error is only logged.
flow-mail-template-incomplete.solution: Open the mail templates in the administration and fill in the subject, the HTML content and the plain text content in the default language.

number-range-type-missing.title: Number ranges without a number range type
number-range-type-missing.description: These number ranges belong to a number range type that does not exist anymore, usually because an extension removed its number range type but left its number ranges behind. Shopware never uses these number ranges, they are leftovers.
number-range-type-missing.solution: Delete the number ranges, for example through the Admin API, or reinstall the extension that provided the number range type.

number-range-sales-channel-missing.title: Number range types without a number range for a sales channel
number-range-sales-channel-missing.description: For these combinations of an active storefront or headless sales channel and a number range type, there is no number range: none is assigned to the sales channel, and neither the type nor one of its number ranges is global. Shopware cannot generate a number of this type for the sales channel, so for example placing an order, registering a customer or creating a document fails with an error.
number-range-sales-channel-missing.solution: Open the number ranges in the administration and assign a number range of this type to the sales channel, or create a global number range for the type. Types whose number ranges are neither global nor assigned to a sales channel are not counted, because an extension that looks up its number range itself does not resolve them per sales channel. Orders, customers, products and documents are always counted, because Shopware looks up their number ranges by type.

composerAudit.subtitle: Check installed Composer packages against the Packagist security advisories database.

explainer.title: What is this?
explainer.what: Your shop is built from many smaller software building blocks (called "dependencies") — both Shopware itself and the plugins and libraries it uses. This page checks the exact versions installed in your shop against a public database of known security problems.
explainer.why: When a problem (an "advisory") is found, it means a building block your shop relies on has a known weakness that attackers could potentially exploit. The good news: almost all of them are already fixed in a newer version — your shop just needs to be updated to it.
explainer.who: Updating these building blocks is a technical task. If you don't manage your shop's code yourself, send this list (or a screenshot) to your developer or agency and ask them to apply the updates — the step-by-step instructions below are written for them.

howto.title: How to fix these advisories
howto.backup: Always create a full backup (database and files) before updating dependencies, so you can roll back if an update breaks your shop.
howto.step1: On your local or CI environment, update the affected packages with Composer. The command below names exactly the packages with advisories; "--with-dependencies" lets Composer also update their required sub-dependencies when a patched version needs it, while leaving the rest of your project untouched:
howto.step2: Review the changes (especially major version bumps) and run your test suite to catch regressions.
howto.step4: Commit the updated composer.lock and deploy. The check above re-runs automatically (cached up to 1 hour — use Refresh to force it).
howto.note: Some advisories are fixed only in a newer major version. If a constraint in your composer.json blocks the update, you may need to raise it (e.g. "^2.0") before Composer can install the patched release.

communication.title: How apps communicate with your shop
communication.intro: Apps with an external backend run their logic on the app provider’s servers. Your shop and the app server need to communicate in both directions. This also applies to Shopware Services, which are based on the app system and rely on the same shop reachability and Shop App ID.
communication.shopDescription: Provides shop data through the Admin API.
communication.inbound: App → shop: API requests via APP_URL
communication.serverDescription: Processes events and reads or updates shop data within the app’s granted permissions.
communication.identity: Recognizes your installation by its Shop App ID.
communication.caption: For example: an order event triggers a webhook to the app. The app then calls your shop’s API to retrieve order details.
communication.reachabilityTitle: Why the shop must be reachable
communication.reachabilityDescription: The app server must be able to reach your APP_URL over the internet using HTTPS. Localhost, a private network, or a firewall or HTTP password protection that blocks app requests prevents it from calling back. Being able to open the shop in your own browser is not enough. API access still requires authentication and the app’s permissions.
communication.uniqueIdTitle: One installation, one Shop App ID
communication.uniqueIdDescription: The Shop App ID identifies the installation to app servers. Production, staging and development installations must each have a different ID; sharing one can cause app servers to confuse the shops and their data.
communication.copyHint: When copying a shop, give the copy its own APP_URL and Shop App ID before using apps. Moving the same shop to a new domain keeps its identity.
